elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates without an additional notice condition.
elements.evidence: The grant covers only an affiliate “identified in written notice to Kubient,” so affiliate coverage is conditional on notice.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause does not grant licence rights to Customer's contractors.
The clause does not state that any paid-up licence is perpetual. “Royalty-free” does not demonstrate that a paid-up licence cannot exist, and no duration protection is included.
The licence is expressly described as “revocable,” without an exception for paid-up licences.

elements.element: Any subscription licence may be terminated only for an uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The grant remains broadly revocable and contains no material-breach trigger, cure requirement, or limitation on termination of a subscription licence. The subscription condition is not demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors without limitation to a specified transaction type.
elements.evidence: Transferability is limited to a successor arising by “merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets,” rather than successors generally.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered when identified in written notice.
elements.evidence: The licence is granted directly to “any affiliate of Customer identified in written notice to Kubient.”

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The licence is expressly “transferable to a successor of Customer by merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets.”

result.reason: The operative redline fully reaches the fallback by covering notified affiliates and permitting transfer to an M&A successor. It does not reach the preferred position because affiliate coverage requires notice, contractors are omitted, the licence remains revocable, no perpetual or breach-and-cure protections are added, and transferability is transaction-limited. The changes are confined to those needed for the fallback and are consistent with the existing assignment provision.
